problem: Interactive imitation policies need help in unfamiliar or dangerous states, but frequent context switches impose human burden even when each correction is short.
contribution: Robot-gated intervention based jointly on novelty and learned failure risk, with asymmetric enter/exit thresholds and an explicit intervention budget.
algorithm: Train a bootstrapped policy ensemble; average action-component variance estimates novelty. A goal-probability critic estimates task failure risk. Enter supervisor mode for high novelty or high risk; cede only when both human-policy action discrepancy and risk are low. Data quantiles adapt thresholds to the requested budget.
observations: Generic state inputs in simulated peg insertion; the physical cable-routing policy observes workspace RGB at64x64, rather than privileged contact state.
actions: Continuous planar delta positions in the physical daVinci cable task; human teleoperation targets supply correction labels.
embodiment_and_data: Simulated peg insertion, a three-robot simulated fleet with10human participants, and physical cable routing. The physical task starts from25demonstrations/1381state-action pairs and collects1500environment steps.
experiments: Autonomous success after training is evaluated separately from intervention-aided success. Fleet study measures switching, actions, throughput, idle time and concurrent human-task performance. Some burden metrics are explicitly conditional on successful episodes, so they cannot replace all-attempt success accounting.
baselines: Behavior cloning, HG-DAgger, SafeDAgger and LazyDAgger; physical table comparesBC, HG-DAgger andThriftyDAgger.

quantitative_result.note: Do not equate intervention-aided15/15 with autonomous performance.

limitations: Risk estimates are trusted only near familiar states; policy variance is not a calibrated safety certificate. Budget-sensitive thresholds and available human response remain assumptions. Simulated fleet evidence is not a physical three-robot deployment.
hardware_adaptation: Compare novelty/risk gating in simulation and use it only to request supervision. It cannot override independentNano/Pi limits, STOP or lease. NX resource cost of an ensemble must be measured.
algorithm_detail: Novelty is bootstrap ensemble action variance; risk is1minus a learned discounted goal-success estimate. Entering uses anOR of novelty/risk; returning uses anAND of low disagreement and lowrisk with stricter thresholds, implementing hysteresis. This avoids confusing uncertain unfamiliar states with well-known but failure-prone bottlenecks.
integration_contract: Intervention requests, human acceptance, ownership transfer and eventual ceding need separate timestamped events. A requested human response is not an executed correction; timeout remains a local safe stop. Keep aided and autonomous episode outcomes distinct.
license_evidence: The primaryPMLR paper and PDF were read. No official sourcecode or code license was verified, so the decision authorizes conceptual comparison, not copying code.
required_experiments: Known-fault simulation ablations for novelty-only/risk-only/both; compare matched expert-query budgets and full-task outcomes; test absent operator and delayed handoff; measure abstention/calibration and all safety stops.
difference_from_explorer: This already addresses intervention scheduling; a human-time saving alone is not Explorer's main scientific contribution. Cause identification, cross-embodiment effects and retention require additional evidence.
